state.output:
---
name: free-vision
description: Use when the user asks to describe/analyze/read an image, screenshot, photo, or a picture in code. Covers the vision models that need no API key (OpenCode Zen mimo-v2-omni-free, Kilo 200 req/h, OVH 2 req/min, plus fallbacks). Use when asked "what's on the image", OCR of screens, UI mockups, diagram reading.
---

# Free vision models (no API key)

## Шаг 0 — сначала проверь, не видишь ли ты сам

Это правило важнее всех остальных в этом файле. **Никогда не зови внешний движок,
если ты сам работаешь на модели с вижном.**

```bash
bash .opencode/skills/free-vision/can-see.sh "<твоя-модель-id>"
```

- exit 0 → **читай картинку сам** инструментом `read`. Всё. Ни base64, ни curl,
  ни делегирования: ты уже видишь её, а внешний вызов — это лишний расход,
  лишний rate-limit и лишнее ожидание.
- exit 1 → модель текстовая, тогда и примени эту инструкцию: субагент `vision`
  или один из эндпоинтов ниже.

Список всех vision-моделей конфига: `bash .opencode/skills/free-vision/can-see.sh`.

Команда читает флаг `attachment` из resolved-конфига opencode, так что ответ —
факт, а не догадка. У bare-id модели (`mimo-v2-omni-free`) тоже работает.

**Только когда exit 1** — дальше по списку ниже. Шаг 0 не опционален: агент
регулярно нырял в curl к Kilo/OVH с картинкой, которую видел сам.

Бесплатные вижн-модели **без ключа и регистрации**. Проверено 22.09.2026 (живой запрос с изображением). Источник: `free-multimodal-models.txt` в корне репозитория.

## Правила
- **Сначала Шаг 0.** Видишь сам — читай сам, внешние движки не трогай.
- Эндпоинты Kilo/OVH анонимные: **НЕ добавляй заголовок `Authorization`** (иначе 401).
- Изображение передаётся как data URL: `data:image/png;base64,....` (jpg → `data:image/jpeg;base64,...`).
- Парс ответа: `choices[0].message.content`. У Kilo может прийти `reasoning` — бери итоговый `content`.

## 0. OpenCode Zen (основной, внутри opencode)
Модель: `opencode/mimo-v2-omni-free` (текст + изображения + аудио).
- Бесплатно, без ключа, **только внутри opencode** (мы внутри — работает нативно).
- Базовый URL: `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1` (OpenAI-compatible).
- Используй нативно: `model: opencode/mimo-v2-omni-free`.

## 1. Kilo Code Gateway (внешний фоллбэк, 200 req/ч)
`POST https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/v1/chat/completions`

```bash
DATA_URL="data:image/jpeg;base64,...."
curl -s https://api.kilo.ai/api/gateway/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Опиши фото подробно\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"$DATA_URL\"}}]}],\"max_tokens\":3000}" \
  | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['choices'][0]['message']['content'])"
```

Вижн-модели Kilo (`:free`):
- `stepfun/step-3.7-flash:free` — текст + изображения (основная)
- `nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-omni-30b-a3b-reasoning:free` — + аудио
- `dots-studio/dots-3-note-preview:free`
- `inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-vl:free` — бывает 429, повторить
- `nex-agi/nex-n2.5-pro:free`
- `inclusionai/ling-3.0-flash-sante:free`

## 2. OVHcloud AI (резерв, 2 req/мин)
`POST https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1/chat/completions`
- Модель: `Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct` (текст + изображения, отвечает по-русски).
- Жёсткий rate-limit 2/мин: при 429 ждать 60+ сек.

```bash
curl -s https://oai.endpoints.kepler.ai.cloud.ovh.net/v1/chat/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"model\":\"Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct\",\"messages\":[{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":[{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Опиши фото подробно\"},{\"type\":\"image_url\",\"image_url\":{\"url\":\"$DATA_URL\"}}]}],\"max_tokens\":1500}"
```

## 3. Резерв
- **VisionSter** (сторонняя обёртка, модель не раскрыта): `POST https://ahm7xmakki.com/api/imgchat` с JSON `{"userPrompt":"...","image":"data:image/jpeg;base64,...","messages":[...]}`. Агрессивный rate-limit.

## Не путать — текстовые (без вижн) в этих провайдерах
- Kilo текст: `nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free`, `z-ai/glm-5.2:free` (на картинку 404), `qwen/qwen3.8-27b:free`, `thinkingmachines/inkling-small:free`, etc.
- OpenCode Zen free текст: `deepseek-v4-flash-free`, `mimo-v2.5-free`, `kimi-k2.5-free`, `nemotron-3-ultra-free` — строго текст (вижн только `mimo-v2-omni-free`).

The flow: When the user presses "Запустить хаб":
1. If there's an active hub run → `tryOpenLive(token)` 
2. `tryOpenLive` reads the session file; if state==='live' and has hubUrl → probes candidates
3. If NO reachable base → logs "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" and returns false → **dead end, requires manual restart**

That's the critical bug shown in the screenshots: the app gets stuck in a loop where it says "Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв — ран, скорее всего, остановлен извне). Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер»." — and the user must manually click restart.

Critical issue #2: `readHubSessionRaw` — the raw.githubusercontent.com edge cache is stale by minutes. The comment at line 629-634 acknowledges this. But `tryOpenLive` at line 542 calls `readHubSessionRaw()` **only** — it never falls back to `readHubSessionViaApi`. So if the raw edge serves a stale `ended` file from a previous run (or a stale live file with a dead address), `tryOpenLive` reads STALE data forever and never gets fresh data. That's a genuine bug: `tryOpenLive` should use `readHubSession(token)` not `readHubSessionRaw()`.

Critical issue #3: `raw.githubusercontent.com` **does not serve the `session-state` branch by default** unless the branch is published... actually raw serves any branch ref. But it requires the repo to be public. If the repo is private, raw returns 404. Then it falls to the API path. OK.

Meanwhile the "Последние запуски" card showed **NPM Hub Build #385 running for 5h33m** — i.e. the GitHub Actions run IS alive. So: run alive, but the panel can never reconnect. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв)…" → dead end, must manually press "Остановить и перезапустить ранер".

2. "хочу чтобы аи мог работать автоматически без моего вмешательства" — the panel must recover on its own, no manual button presses.
3. Earlier user asked: can the runner live in Docker so they connect by IP? (Not the main ask now; just context that they want the runner always-on and reachable by a stable address.)
4. Earlier: agent needs full access including /tmp, download and install packages — so full-auto operation must not be sandboxed away.

## Code facts I already established (verify, don't trust blindly)

- `tryOpenLive(token)` — index.html:541. Called from `runHubFlow('launch')` when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'` (index.html:1001-1008).
- `tryOpenLive` line 542 reads the session file via **`readHubSessionRaw()` ONLY** — never the authenticated API path.
- `readHubSessionRaw()` — index.html:591 — fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO}/session-state/{live/session-hub-linux.json, session-hub-linux.json}?t=<cachebust>`, no token.
- The file itself already documents (index.html:629-634) that **raw.githubusercontent.com serves edge copies that can be minutes stale**, and that `waitForHub()` therefore switches to the REST contents API after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). **`tryOpenLive` has no such fallback.**
- Consequence A: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'ended'` file → prints the exact 01:25:16 message "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" → returns false, even though the hub is live and its address is published. Dead end.
- Consequence B: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'live'` file holding the PREVIOUS run's dead ngrok URL → probes it → "Failed to fetch" → prints the exact 01:21:03 message "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" → returns false. Dead end.
- `firstReachableBase(bases, ztOrCandidates, runId)` — index.html:685. Walks bases × token candidates, returns `{base, zt, errors}`; every failure reason is collected in `errors[]`.
- When ALL probes fail with network-class reasons (`/failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed/i`), `tryOpenLive` lines 554-557 concludes "туннель мёртв" and tells the user to press the restart button manually. No automatic action is taken, even though `restartRunner(token, zt, runner)` (index.html:573) and `cancelAndWait(token)` (index.html:527) exist on the very same page and do exactly the needed work.
- `runHubFlow('launch')` lines 1005-1008: when `tryOpenLive` returns false it calls `progFinish(false, 'Доступ не подошёл — хаб закрыт чужим токеном запуска. Нажми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».')` — i.e. the false diagnosis "чужим токеном" is printed even when the real cause was a dead tunnel or a stale read.
- `openLast()` — index.html:858 — only probes `last.url` and `last.reserve` from localStorage. It never re-reads the session file, so the "Открыть последний (N мин назад)" button can never self-heal. It throws "Последний хаб недоступен: ..." (and via index.html:1318-1319 the generic "Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв" text).

Neither function compares `updated_at`/`runId` to pick the freshest.
- `sessionBases(s)` — index.html:842 — order is `s.ngrok`, then `s.hubUrl || s.url`, then `s.url2`.
- `hubCandidates(s)` — index.html:813 — produces token candidates incl. a `spare` derived from the GitHub token via `sha256Hex`.
- `waitForHub(token, sinceMs, sleepMs, cancelled, runId)` — index.html:614 — the good pattern: raw first, API fallback after 3 stale reads, plus `runGone()` to notice external cancellation, 240 iterations.

2. **Any additional critical bug in this same code path that I missed.** Look hard at: stale-vs-fresh session-file selection, the `live/` vs flat path precedence, what happens across a page reload mid-launch (`savePending`/`readPending`/`clearPending` at index.html:728-735 — `clearPending` is called on success at 567 and 958, but is the pending zt ever *used* on a later open?), the auto-lock IIFE at index.html:887-912 (it reads the module-scope `nowMs` — is that ever updated? Be concrete and cite line numbers. If you think I'm wrong about something, say so bluntly.

## Verdict

Your six findings are **4 confirmed, 1 wrong, 1 moot** — but they are not the worst of it. The panel has a fully implemented, whitelisted remote-repair channel on the runner (`control/queue.json` with a `reopen-tunnel` op, `tools/hub_control.sh:22,119-135`) that the panel **never touches** (`grep control/ hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` → zero hits). That is the correct answer to "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead", it costs1 branch write, and it kills nothing. Everything else in this design is secondary to wiring it up.

---

## 1. Your six findings

**#1 `tryOpenLive` reads raw only — CONFIRMED.** `:542` `const s = await readHubSessionRaw();`. `readHubSessionRaw` (`:591-599`) is raw.githubusercontent only, no token, no API fallback. `waitForHub` has the stale→API switch at `:639` (`token && staleReads >= 3`). `tryOpenLive` has nothing. Settled.

**#2 Consequence A (stale `ended` → the 01:25:16 line) — CONFIRMED.** `:543-546` collapses `!s`, `s.state!=='live'` and `!(s.hubUrl||s.url)` into one message at `:544`. That is the exact 01:25:16 string, verbatim.

**#3 Consequence B (stale `live` with a dead URL → 01:21:03) — CONFIRMED.** `:551-562`, message at `:557` is verbatim.

**#4 No auto-action on total network failure — CONFIRMED.** `:554-557` prints and returns `false`. `restartRunner` (`:573`) and `cancelAndWait` (`:527`) are on the page. **But note: `restartRunner` is dead code — grep shows zero call sites.** The live restart path is an inline duplicate at `:986-998`. So "the function that does the needed work exists" is true only of `cancelAndWait`; there are two copies of the destructive operation and only one of them is wired.

**#5 `openLast` never re-reads the session file — CONFIRMED.** `:858-880` probes `last.url`, then `last.reserve`, then throws. Worse than you said: it probes with **one** token, `lastOriginToken().zt` (`:860`) — no pending, no spare, no `hubCandidates`. Even with a fresh file it would 401 after a storage wipe.

**#6 `readSlotRaw` first-wins is a hazard — WRONG IN PRACTICE. Drop this one.** Nothing writes the flat path any more: `tools/publish_session.sh` `layout_file()` maps `session*.json → live/…`, and the `file=` override whitelist (publish_session.sh, the `[[ "$FILE_OVERRIDE" =~ … ]]` block) accepts only `models-*`, `audit/code`, `chats/`, `saved-`, `history/` — **no session names**. `migrate_session_state.sh` only `git mv`s old ones into `live/`. So `live/` is unconditionally the newer file; the precedence is correct. The staleness that actually bites you is the CDN edge copy of `live/` itself, which P0 below fixes. Changing this would be churn for a case that cannot occur.

**Your two open questions, both no-ops:** `nowMs` (`:833`) is a one-shot evaluated at load, immediately after `let last = readLast()` (`:832`), and the only consumer is the `age` at `:889` — correct. The ticking branch at `:901` correctly uses `Date.now()`. Not frozen. And `tokenNow()` is defined at `:1140` as a hoisted function declaration, well before `openSlot` (`:1237`) ever runs. Both fine.

---

## 2. What you missed (ranked)

1. **The runner-side repair channel exists and is unused.** `tools/hub_control.sh` runs a 20 s daemon publishing `control/heartbeat-hub.json` (2-min process census: `hub_server`, `cloudflared`, `tunnel_keeper`, `ngrok_keeper`) and executing `control/queue.json` `{seq, op, target}` against a whitelist including **`reopen-tunnel`** (kills cloudflared, reopens, writes `hub-url`, and **republishes the session descriptor** — `publish_url`, so the panel's next raw read gets the new URL). `restart-hub` and `up-hub` are there too. The panel writes nothing to `control/`.

2. **`openSlot`'s failure message is unconditionally wrong.** `:1302` passes `candidates[candidates.length-1] || ''` as the `zt` argument. `hubCandidates` always ends with the open gate `''` (`:826`), so `zt` is **always** `''` → `describeBaseFailure` always takes the `!String(zt||'')` branch (`:709`) and always prints «Нет токена запуска (zt): адрес отвечает 401» — even when a launch token existed and was rejected. Branches `:712-714` are unreachable from this call site.

3. **`detectSessionConflict` throws away the run it just fetched.** `:532-537` reduces a full run object to the string `'hub'`, and `runHubFlow` (`:1002`) discards it. Meanwhile `s.runId` in the session file is sitting right there, and `preflightHub` already arbitrates on `j.runId` (`:672`). A free, decisive staleness signal — *does the file's runId equal the active run's id* — is being thrown away every time.

4. **There are no timeouts anywhere.** `api()` `:322`, `readHubSessionRaw` `:594`, `preflightHub` `:667` — all bare `fetch`. A half-open TCP connect blocks the probe loop indefinitely. Fatal for any watchdog.

5. **`prog-stop` doesn't stop anything and un-greys buttons mid-flight.** `progAbort` is created at `:280` and **never passed to any fetch**. `:1037` re-enables `launch`/`restart` while the flow is still awaiting, so a second `runHubFlow` can start; both will `location.href`. Same class: `autoPending` (`:1396-1405`) fires `tryOpenLive` unawaited and unlocked, racing `autoLock`'s 3-second `openLast()` (`:900`).

6. **Only two tunnel legs existed in your run.** One «пробую резервный…» line (`:689`, only for `i>0`) ⇒ `sessionBases` returned exactly 2 bases ⇒ `s.ngrok` was empty. Either `NGROK_AUTHTOKEN` is empty (hub.yml prints `::notice::NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty - the ngrok reserve leg is off`) or the keeper died. Worth checking that run's log before blaming the panel.

7. **`hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` is not syntax-checked by CI.** `js-syntax.yml` extracts and `node --check`s the inline script of `agent/hub/index.html` — a *different* page (`<title>Zen Agent</title>`, 1331 lines). Your file, the one on the phone, has no syntax gate at all.

---

## 3. Design, in priority order

**P0 — one honest, authenticated session read.** Extract `readSessionFresh(token, {activeRunId})` → `{s, src, err}` where `src ∈ {raw,api,none}` and `err ∈ {offline, notfound, unauthorized, http}`. It must (a) fetch **both** paths and keep both results, picking the greater `Date.parse(startedAt)` with `runNumber` as tie-break; (b) if the winner's `runId` ≠ `activeRunId`, spend exactly **one** `readHubSessionViaApi` call and prefer that; (c) only return `notfound` when both paths genuinely 404'd — a thrown fetch is `offline`, never `notfound`. `readHubSessionRaw` stays as a thin wrapper so `readHubSession` (`:609`) and the existing suite keep working.

**P1 — `detectSessionConflict` returns `{kind, run}`; `tryOpenLive(token, run)` uses it.** Three lines, the highest value-per-line change in the file. Then inside `tryOpenLive`: drop the `:543` early-out. If `s.runId !== run.id` → «файл сессии от прошлого рана; текущий #N ещё не опубликовал адрес» and fall into the wait path. If `!s` → report `offline`/`notfound` distinctly, never «туннель мёртв».

**P2 — the repair ladder `recoverLive(token, s, run)` → `{ok, base, url, action}`.** Ordered, and the ordering *is* the safety argument:

1. One API re-read + re-probe. (1 quota, 0 destructive.)
2. **Enqueue `reopen-tunnel`**: `GET` `control/queue.json` for the sha, `PUT {seq: Date.now(), op:'reopen-tunnel', target:'hub', from:'panel'}`. Then poll raw (free) every 10 s for ≤120 s for a changed `url`/`ngrok`; on change, re-probe. (2 quota, 0 destructive, keeps the 5h33m run, its repos and its terminals.) If `control/heartbeat-hub.json` is missing or >6 min stale, skip to step 3 — nothing on the runner can heal itself.
3. Only then restart — through `restartRunner` (`:573`), never the inline duplicate at `:986-998`.

**Gate for P2 step 3 — all five must hold:** `isHubRun(run)`; no non-hub session run in `listActiveRuns(isSessionRun)`; `GET /actions/runs/{runId}` confirms an ACTIVE status **twice, 60 s apart** (so a transient API blip can't trigger it); `localStorage.hub_autorepair === '1'`; and a persisted budget of ≤3 restarts / 24 h. Never within 10 min of a run's birth.

**Answer to your explicit question — run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead:** step 2. Reopen the tunnel on the live runner. `tunnel_keeper.sh` already tries this on its own (`MAIN_FAILS >= 3` → `open_main` → `publish_pair`), so often the fresh URL is already on the branch and the panel just never re-read it. The ladder makes the panel a participant instead of a bystander. A restart is the last resort, and by then the blast radius is already bounded: `backup-work.sh` every 300 s and `auto-ship.sh` every 180 s per repo (hub.yml), so the worst case is minutes of unshipped diff — not five hours of session.

**P3 — `runHubFlow`'s message (`:1012`).** Make `tryOpenLive` return `{ok, reason}` with `reason ∈ {opened, offline, notfound, stale-file, still-booting, dead-tunnel, token-mismatch, run-gone}` and one honest sentence each. The string «закрыт чужим токеном запуска» may only appear when at least one probe received an actual HTTP 401 from a hub that answered — today's `:555` regex cannot tell those apart from a dead socket.

**P4 — `openLast` (`:858`) gets the same fallback.** After both stored bases fail: fresh read → `firstReachableBase(sessionBases(s), await hubCandidates(s), s.runId)` → `saveLast` → navigate. This is what actually kills the manual loop, because the 3-second auto-open (`:900`) goes through it.

**P5 — a watchdog, journal-only.** On load, on `visibilitychange`, on `online`: if `readLast()` exists and `!document.hidden`, every 45 s read the session file raw (free). If `s.runId` differs from the one recorded in `hub_last`, or the current base fails two preflights in a row, run the ladder. Single-flight, abortable. **It must never touch `prog*`** — only the journal and a small badge, or it will stomp on a user's in-flight flow.

**P6 — the plumbing the above needs.** One `let flow = null` mutex across `runHubFlow`/`openSlot`/`openLast`/`tryOpenLive`/`autoPending`/`autoLock`; thread `progAbort.signal` into `api()` and `preflightHub` plus `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)`; stop `:1037` from re-enabling buttons until the flow actually returns.

**Explicitly not doing:** reordering `readSlotRaw` (see #6 above), and any "try more hosts" fallback — see risks.

---

## 4. Risks

- **Token safety.** The spare is a real run-scoped credential (it opens the gate). `firstReachableBase` sends *every* candidate to *every* base, so adding bases multiplies exposure. Hard rule for the ladder: **no host outside the session file is ever contacted**, and the queue write goes only to `api.github.com`. Do not add a fallback host list.
- **Quota.** P0 costs ≤1 request per reconnect, not per poll — keep it that way. The real bomb is `waitForRunsToStop` (`:513`, default **400 attempts × 3 s**); when called from auto-repair pass explicit small args. Also kill the fire-and-forget `followRun` at `:942` when the flow ends — it currently keeps polling for 7.5 min after a *successful* open, which compounds badly under a repeating loop.
- **Progress UI.** Any watchdog calling `progStart`/`progFinish` will fight the user. Restrict it to the journal.
- **Offline.** Every tier degrades silently: `navigator.onLine === false` or a failed raw read ⇒ skip the tick, no error, no `progFinish`, no budget spend. A phone in a lift must not accumulate red journal lines.
- **Suite regressions.** `hub-connect-e2e.js` `c16` asserts `cands.list.length === 2` and `c17` calls `window.tryOpenLive('ghp_x')` with one argument — P1 must keep `run` optional. And with `describeBaseFailure`'s call site fixed, `c12b/c13/c14` still pass (they call it directly) but `c18`'s expectation about the openSlot message changes.

---

## 5. Test plan

Tooling: **jsdom, Node, no deps beyond `jsdom`** — `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` already loads this exact `index.html` (`:5`), stubs `fetch` (`:19`), and drives `tryOpenLive` directly (`c17`). Extend that file; do not create a new harness.

Stub additions needed: a mutable `liveSession` (already exists), a second `contents` branch shape for the flat path, a recorder for `PUT /contents/control/queue.json`, a recorder for `GET .../contents/control/heartbeat-hub.json`, and a `logs` array fed from `#log` after each call.

| id | case |
|---|---|
| `t1` | active run id ≠ file `runId` ⇒ no «ещё не сообщил» line, no `return false` |
| `t2` | raw returns stale, contents returns fresh ⇒ the fresh one wins |
| `t3` | both raw paths parse, `live/` older ⇒ assert the chosen contract explicitly |
| `t4` | both fetches throw ⇒ `err === 'offline'`, **not** `'notfound'` |
| `t5` | all bases dead, run active, heartbeat fresh ⇒ `cancelOrder.length === 0` **and** one `reopen-tunnel` PUT recorded |
| `t6` | after the PUT the next raw poll returns a new url ⇒ returns true, `hub_last` carries the new base |
| `t7` | heartbeat stale + run confirmed active twice + opt-in + budget ⇒ exactly one cancel, one dispatch |
| `t8` | same, budget exhausted ⇒ zero cancels |
| `t9` | openSlot failure with a launch token present ⇒ message names the mismatch, not «нет zt» |
| `t10` | `openLast`, both stored bases dead, fresh live file ⇒ true, `hub_last` updated |
| `t11` | two overlapping watchdog triggers ⇒ one reconcile (count probe calls) |
| `t12` | `prog-stop` mid-`waitForRunsToStop` ⇒ flow aborts, buttons stay disabled until it returns |

Plus one CI fix: add `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` to the inline-script extractor in `.github/workflows/js-syntax.yml` — today only `agent/hub/index.html` is checked, and that is a different page.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong
#   assumption: the workflow starts TWO VMs (hub web + VNC desktop) and the
#   hub VM's agent itself can die, taking every step with it while detached
#   daemons keep breathing. So now:
#     - BOTH VMs run this daemon, each with its own CONTROL_TARGET
#     - liveness is verifiable from outside: control/heartbeat-<vm>.json is
#       rewritten every 2 minutes with a process census
#     - this daemon can REPAIR, not only report: reopen-tunnel and up-hub fix
#       the exact failure mode of a dead cloudflared / dead hub server without
#       needing the job's keep-alive step at all
#
# CHANNEL (session-state branch)
#   control/queue.json             one slot: { seq, op, target?, from? }
#                                  target = hub | vnc | any (default any)
#   control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json per-VM ack
#   control/heartbeat-<vm>.json    liveness + process census every 2 min
#
# WHITELIST (never arbitrary shell)
#   ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel
set -uo pipefail

HUB_LOGS="${HUB_LOGS:-$HOME/.npm-hub/logs}"
mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
VM="${CONTROL_TARGET:-hub}"
log() { echo "[hub-control:$VM $(date -u '+%H:%M:%S')] $*" | tee -a "$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.log"; }

TOKEN="${GH_TOKEN:-${GITHUB_TOKEN:-}}"
if [ -z "$TOKEN" ]; then
  log "no token - the command queue stays cold"
  exit 1
fi
REPO="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-sj0404-collab/zen-panel}"
BRANCH="${CONTROL_BRANCH:-session-state}"
INTERVAL="${CONTROL_INTERVAL:-20}"
HEARTBEAT_SEC="${CONTROL_HEARTBEAT_SEC:-120}"
API="https://api.github.com/repos/$REPO/contents"
QUEUE_PATH="control/queue.json"
SEEN_FILE="$HUB_LOGS/hub-control-$VM.seen"
SEEN="$(cat "$SEEN_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
TOOLS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
HUB_PORT="${HUB_PORT:-8090}"

trap 'log "stopped"; exit 0' TERM INT

api_get() {
  local body
  body="$(curl -sf -m 20 -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1?ref=$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
  echo "$body"
}

api_put() {
  local b64 sha
  b64="$(printf '%s' "$2" | base64 -w0)"
  sha="$(api_get "$1" | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin).get("sha",""))' 2>/dev/null || echo)"
  if [ -n "$sha" ]; then
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\",\"sha\":\"$sha\"}" >/dev/null
  else
    curl -sf -m 25 -X PUT -H "Authorization: token $TOKEN" "$API/$1" \
      -d "{\"message\":\"control: ack $1\",\"content\":\"$b64\",\"branch\":\"$BRANCH\"}" >/dev/null
  fi
}

publish_url() {  # $1 = slot, $2 = new tunnel base url (no trailing slash)
  local slot="$1" base="$2" rv
  if [ "$slot" = "hub-linux" ]; then
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=hub-linux" "kind=NPM-Hub" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base" "hubUrl=$base" "desktop=$base/d" "mobile=$base/m" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "auth=без пароля" "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  else
    rv="$(cat "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url2" 2>/dev/null || true)"
    GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" bash "$TOOLS_DIR/publish_session.sh" \
      "slot=vnc" "kind=Linux-VNC" "os=linux" \
      "url=$base/vnc.html" "novncUrl=$base/vnc.html" \
      ${rv:+"url2=$rv"} \
      "label=${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" 2>&1 | tail -1
  fi
}

run_op() {
  local pid url
  case "$1" in
    ping)
      echo "pong from $VM $(date -Iseconds)"
      ;;
    backup-now)
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/backup-work.sh" --once
      ;;
    restart-hub)
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      if [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill "$pid" && echo "hub pid $pid signalled"
      else
        echo "no live hub pid (already down?)"
      fi
      ;;
    up-hub)
      if [ "$VM" != "hub" ]; then echo "the npm-hub server lives on the hub VM not $VM"; return 0; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null && { echo "hub already running (pid $pid)"; return 0; }
      (
        cd "$TOOLS_DIR/../npm-hub" || exit 1
        HUB_PORT_STRICT=1 HUB_TOKEN="${HUB_TOKEN_VALUE:-}" HUB_LABEL="${HUB_LABEL:-hub}" \
          GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" PORT="$HUB_PORT" \
          SESSION_STARTED_MS="$(cat "$HOME/.npm-hub/session-start" 2>/dev/null || date +%s000)" \
          SESSION_LIMIT_MS=21600000 nohup node src/server.js >> "$HUB_LOGS/hub.log" 2>&1 &
        echo $! > "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid"
      )
      sleep 2; echo "hub relaunched (pid $(cat "$HUB_LOGS/hub.pid" 2>/dev/null))"
      ;;
    reopen-tunnel)
      local port slot
      if [ "$VM" = "hub" ]; then port=8090; slot=hub-linux; else port=6081; slot=vnc; fi
      pid="$(tr -dc '0-9' < "$HUB_LOGS/cloudflared-$port.pid" 2>/dev/null || true)"
      [ -n "${pid:-}" ] && kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
      pkill -f "cloudflared [t]unnel --url http://127.0.0.1:$port" 2>/dev/null || true
      sleep 1
      url="$(bash "$TOOLS_DIR/open_tunnel.sh" "$port" "$HUB_LOGS/control-tunnel.log" 2>/dev/null || echo)"
      if [ -z "$url" ]; then echo "open_tunnel gave no URL"; return 1; fi
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] && echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/hub-url" || echo "$url" > "$HUB_LOGS/vnc-url"
      echo "tunnel up: $url"
      publish_url "$slot" "$url"
      ;;
    handoff-save)
      [ "$VM" = "hub" ] || { echo "handoff-save runs on the hub VM"; return 0; }
      GH_TOKEN="$TOKEN" GITHUB_TOKEN="$TOKEN" WORK_BACKUP_ROOT="$HOME" \
        bash "$TOOLS_DIR/handoff.sh"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "unknown op: $1" >&2
      return 64
      ;;
  esac
}

heartbeat() {
  local hb
  hb="$(python3 - <<PYH 2>/dev/null || echo ""
import json, subprocess, datetime
def pc(pat):
    try:
        return subprocess.run(["pgrep","-fc",pat], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10).stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "?"
print(json.dumps({
    "vm": "$VM", "runId": "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}",
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "procs": {
        "hub_server": pc("node src/server.js"),
        "cloudflared": pc("cloudflared [t]unnel"),
        "backup_daemon": pc("[b]ackup-work.sh"),
        "snapshot_daemon": pc("[s]napshot-audit-code.sh"),
        "control_daemon": pc("[h]ub_control.sh"),
        "rescue_ssh": pc("[r]escue_ssh.sh"),
        "tunnel_keeper": pc("[t]unnel_keeper.sh"),
        "ngrok_keeper": pc("[n]grok_keeper.sh"),
    },
}, ensure_ascii=False))
PYH
)"
  [ -n "$hb" ] && api_put "control/heartbeat-$VM.json" "$hb" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
}

log "queue daemon up ($VM) on $BRANCH:$QUEUE_PATH (every ${INTERVAL}s; seen=$SEEN)"
boot_slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
if [ -n "$boot_slot" ]; then
  boot_seq="$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; print(json.loads(base64.b64decode(json.load(sys.stdin)["content"])).get("seq",0))' <<<"$boot_slot" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)"
  if [[ "$boot_seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && [ "$boot_seq" -gt "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null; then
    SEEN="$boot_seq"; echo "$SEEN" > "$SEEN_FILE"
    log "queue baseline set to #$SEEN (stale command - not executing)"
  fi
fi
heartbeat
LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
while true; do
  sleep "$INTERVAL"
  if [ $((SECONDS - LAST_BEAT)) -ge "$HEARTBEAT_SEC" ]; then
    heartbeat; LAST_BEAT=$SECONDS
  fi
  slot="$(api_get "$QUEUE_PATH" || true)"
  [ -n "$slot" ] || continue
  read -r seq op target < <(python3 -c '
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.loads(sys.stdin.read())
    print(int(d.get("seq", 0)), str(d.get("op", ""))[:64], str(d.get("target", "any"))[:16])
except Exception:
    print(0, "", "any")
' <<<"$(python3 -c 'import json,sys,base64; c=json.load(sys.stdin)["content"]; print(base64.b64decode(c).decode(), end="")' <<<"$slot" 2>/dev/null)" 2>/dev/null || echo "0  any")
  [[ "$seq" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
  [ "$seq" -le "$SEEN" ] 2>/dev/null && continue
  [ -n "$op" ] || continue
  { [ "$target" = "any" ] || [ "$target" = "$VM" ]; } || { log "skip #$seq ($op for target=$target)"; echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"; continue; }
  log "command #$seq: $op (target=$target)"
  out="$(run_op "$op" 2>&1 | tail -c 3000)"; rc=$?
  log "command #$seq rc=$rc"
  ack="$(python3 -c '
import json, sys, datetime
print(json.dumps({
    "seq": int(sys.argv[1]), "op": sys.argv[2], "vm": sys.argv[4],
    "ok": sys.argv[3] == "0", "rc": int(sys.argv[3]),
    "at": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ"),
    "runId": sys.argv[5],
    "out": sys.stdin.read()[-2800:],
}, ensure_ascii=False))
' "$seq" "$op" "$rc" "$VM" "${GITHUB_RUN_ID:-local}" <<<"$out" 2>/dev/null || echo "{\"seq\":$seq,\"ok\":false}")"
  if api_put "control/results/$seq-$VM.json" "$ack"; then
    echo "$seq" > "$SEEN_FILE"; SEEN="$seq"
  else
    log "ack push failed - the command WILL rerun until pushed"
  fi
done

# Context: the bug the user is actually hitting

A phone panel user cannot ever reconnect to their hub. Verbatim journal lines from their screenshots:

00:40:56 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...

The panel reads a STALE session file from the raw.githubusercontent.com CDN edge and concludes the tunnel is dead. There is a fully-implemented repair channel on the runner that the panel never uses.

# Root cause (already verified — trust this, but re-read the file to place your edits)

`tryOpenLive(token)` at index.html:541 — reached from `runHubFlow('launch')` at :1001-1008 when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'`:

Compare `waitForHub` at `:639`, which switches to the authenticated REST path after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). The file's own comment at `:629-634` documents that the raw edge serves copies minutes old.
- Line 543-546 collapses `!s`, `state !== 'live'` and missing URL into ONE message — that is the verbatim 01:25:16 line.
- Lines 551-562: when every base × token candidate fails with a network-class reason, it prints the verbatim 01:21:03 line and `return false`. **No action.** But `restartRunner` (`:573`) and `cancelAndWait` (`:527`) are right there on the same page. Note `restartRunner` currently has ZERO call sites (dead code); the live restart is an inline duplicate at `:986-998`.
- `openLast()` (`:858`) probes only the two localStorage bases with a single token (`lastOriginToken().zt`, `:860`) — no pending zt, no spare, no `hubCandidates`, and it never re-reads the session file, so the "Открыть последний" button can never self-heal.
- `detectSessionConflict` (`:532-537`) throws away the run object it just fetched, reducing it to the string `'hub'`. `s.runId` in the session file plus that run's id is a free, decisive staleness signal, and `preflightHub` (`:672`) already arbitrates on exactly `j.runId`.
- `openSlot` (`:1237`) calls `describeBaseFailure(bases, probe.errors, candidates[candidates.length-1] || '', !!spare)` at `:1302`. `hubCandidates` (`:813`) always ends with the open gate `''`, so `zt` is ALWAYS `''` → `describeBaseFailure` (`:709`) always takes the "нет токена запуска" branch. Wrong diagnosis even when a launch token existed and was rejected.

# The thing you must wire up (highest value, do it first)

`tools/hub_control.sh` is a runner-side daemon already executing a whitelisted command queue on the `session-state` branch:

- `control/queue.json` — one slot: `{ seq, op, target?, from? }`; `target` = `hub | vnc | any`; `op` whitelist at `hub_control.sh:23` = `ping, backup-now, handoff-save, restart-hub, up-hub, reopen-tunnel`.
- `control/heartbeat-<vm>.json` — rewritten every 2 min with a process census (`hub_control.sh:144-170`).
- `control/results/<seq>-<vm>.json` — per-VM ack.
- **`reopen-tunnel` (`:119-131`)**: kills cloudflared, calls `open_tunnel.sh` for a fresh URL, writes `$HUB_LOGS/hub-url`, and calls `publish_url` (`:68-85`) → `publish_session.sh` which **republishes the session descriptor with the new URL**. So one queue write repairs a dead tunnel on a live runner and the panel's next raw read picks up the new address.
- The daemon writes the heartbeat via `api_put`, i.e. `PUT /repos/$REPO/contents/<path>?ref=session-state` with `{message, content: base64, branch, sha?}`. `sha` is optional (see `api_put` `:55-66`).

The panel currently contains ZERO references to `control/` (`grep -c 'control/' hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` → 0). Wiring it up is the whole fix.

Panel-side plumbing that already exists: `api(path, token, opts)` at `:322` (supports `method` + `body`, sends `Authorization: token …`, returns `null` on 404, `true` on 202/204); `parseSessionFile(f)` at `:584` (base64→JSON for a contents response); `GH` and `REPO` at `:200`.

# Implement, in this order

## 1. `readSessionFresh(token, opts)` — one honest, authenticated session read

Returns `{ s, src, err }` where `src ∈ {raw, api, none}` and `err ∈ {offline, notfound, stale-file, unauthorized, http}`.

Requirements:
- Fetch **both** paths (`live/session-hub-linux.json`, `session-hub-linux.json`) and keep both results; pick the one with the greater `Date.parse(s.startedAt || s.updated_at || 0)`, tie-break on `runNumber`/`runId`. (Keep `readHubSessionRaw` as a thin wrapper over the raw-only part so `readHubSession` at `:609` and existing tests keep working.)
- If a winner exists and `opts.activeRunId` is set and `String(s.runId) !== String(opts.activeRunId)`: spend exactly ONE `readHubSessionViaApi(token)` call (`:600`) and prefer that result. This is the whole bug: the raw edge is stale.
- A **thrown** fetch is `err: 'offline'`, NEVER `notfound`. Only return `notfound` when both paths genuinely came back 404/failed-to-parse. Offline must never be reported as "сессия не опубликована".
- Do NOT add any fallback host outside the session file. Token safety: the `spare` is a real run-scoped credential that opens the hub gate (`hubCandidates` `:813`, and `SPARE_TOKEN` in `npm-hub/src/server.js`); `firstReachableBase` sends every candidate to every base, so more bases = more exposure.

## 2. `detectSessionConflict` returns `{ kind, run }`

Keep `kind` exactly as today (`'hub'` / `'other'` / `null`) so `runHubFlow` keeps working, and return the run object. Update the one call site at `:1002`. **`tryOpenLive`'s `run` parameter MUST stay optional** — the existing test `tests/hub-connect-e2e.js` case `c17` calls `window.tryOpenLive('ghp_x')` with a single argument.

## 3. `recoverLive(token, s, run)` — the ordered repair ladder

Return `{ ok, base, zt, url, action, reason }`. The ordering IS the safety argument, do not reorder:

**Step 1 — re-read and re-probe.** One `readSessionFresh` + `firstReachableBase`. 1 API request, 0 destructive.

**Step 2 — `reopen-tunnel` on the live runner.** This is the fix for "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead"; it keeps the run, its repos and its terminals.
  a. Read `control/heartbeat-hub.json` (raw, free). If it is missing, unparseable, or its `at` is older than 6 minutes → the daemon is dead, skip to step 3.
  b. `GET /repos/${REPO}/contents/control/queue.json?ref=session-state` via `api()`, decode with `parseSessionFile`, read its `seq`.

# TESTING.md — что нужно провести

Полный план проверок zen-panel: что уже ловится автоматически, что нужно
прогнать руками, и какие поломки известны прямо сейчас.

Документ описывает **проверку**, а не разработку. Каждому пункту дан ID
(`T-xx`), чтобы результат можно было отметить и не потерять.

---

## 0. Текущее состояние (на момент последней правки)

| Область | Состояние |
|---|---|
| `node --check` по JS | зелёный (`JS syntax`) |
| `bash -n` по `tools/*.sh` и всем `run:`-шагам | зелёный (проверено вручную, в CI напрямую нет) |
| 11 сьютов в `tests/` (10 js + 1 shell) | зелёные в CI |
| Из них без зависимостей (7 сьютов) | зелёные локально на Windows: 291 проверка, 1 осознанный skip |
| Сборка APK | зелёная: `v1.299`, `hub-v1.299` (коммит `ab63545`) |
| Живой прогон сессии | подтверждён 26.09: запуск → туннель → отмена → слоты `ended` |
| Живой прогон с `HUB_TOKEN` (gate) | **не проверен** — сервер со стартом на gate вживую не запускался |
| Ручные сценарии (VNC, терминалы, файлы, git, mobile) | **не проводились** |

Пробелы покрытия перечислены в §4.

---

## 1. Уровни проверки

| Уровень | Что ловит | Как запустить | Когда |
|---|---|---|---|
| L0 Синтаксис | опечатки в JS/YAML/sh | `JS syntax` (CI) | на каждый push |
| L1 Регрессия UI | логика панелей и хаба без сети | `Tests` (CI) → `tests/npm test` | на каждый push |
| L2 Shell | синтаксис и логика `tools/*.sh` | `bash -n tools/*.sh`, `tests/work-backup-test.sh` | локально перед коммитом |
| L3 Интеграция | живой runner: туннель, PTY, VNC, gate | ручной прогон сессии | после изменения `npm-hub/src` или workflows |
| L4 Приёмка | сценарий целиком на телефоне | ручной чек-лист §3 | перед релизом APK |

---

### 2.1 Локально

```bash
# регрессия (jsdom; нужен npm ci в tests/)
cd tests && npm ci && npm test

# синтаксис (то же, что делает CI)
for f in tools/*.sh; do bash -n "$f"; done
node --check npm-hub/src/server.js
node --check npm-hub/src/vnc-keepalive.js
node --check npm-hub/src/handoff.js

# проверка YAML всех workflow
python -c "import yaml,glob;[yaml.safe_load(open(f)) for f in glob.glob('.github/workflows/*.yml')]"
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Remote-control + heartbeat daemon for one runner VM (Z10 round 2).
#
# WHY ROUND 2
#   Round 1 proved the queue works, but run 175 showed it lives on the wrong

parts.text:
Repo: /home/runner/work/zen-panel/zen-panel/fork — "Zen Panel", an Android panel + GitHub-Actions-based "NPM Hub" runner. Main UI under test: `hub/src/main/assets/hub/index.html` (single 1408-line file, vanilla JS).

## User report (from phone screenshots, decoded)

The user cannot connect to their hub/runner. Verbatim log lines from the journal:

```
00:37:33 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:39:53 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:40:13 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:40:30 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:40:56 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
00:40:56 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв. Если хаб жив — «Запустить хаб» подберёт доступ, иначе жми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
00:41:48 Список сессий: Failed to fetch
00:41:58 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
00:41:58 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв...

01:19:56 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
01:19:56 Открыть не вышло: Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв...
01:20:20 Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ...
01:21:03 Основной адрес молчит — пробую резервный...
01:21:03 Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв — ран, скорее всего, остановлен извне). Нажмите «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».
01:25:16 Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен). Подожди пару минут и нажми «Запустить хаб» снова — страница подключится к уже идущему.
```

Meanwhile the "Последние запуски" card showed **NPM Hub Build #385 running for 5h33m** — i.e. the GitHub Actions run IS alive. So: run alive, but the panel can never reconnect. The user is trapped in a manual loop: press "Запустить хаб" → "Хаб уже запущен. Подбираю доступ…" → "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв)…" → dead end, must manually press "Остановить и перезапустить ранер".

## User's explicit goals
1. Fix the connection bug so it self-heals.
2. "хочу чтобы аи мог работать автоматически без моего вмешательства" — the panel must recover on its own, no manual button presses.
3. Earlier user asked: can the runner live in Docker so they connect by IP? (Not the main ask now; just context that they want the runner always-on and reachable by a stable address.)
4. Earlier: agent needs full access including /tmp, download and install packages — so full-auto operation must not be sandboxed away.

## Code facts I already established (verify, don't trust blindly)

- `tryOpenLive(token)` — index.html:541. Called from `runHubFlow('launch')` when `detectSessionConflict(token) === 'hub'` (index.html:1001-1008).
- `tryOpenLive` line 542 reads the session file via **`readHubSessionRaw()` ONLY** — never the authenticated API path.
- `readHubSessionRaw()` — index.html:591 — fetches `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/${REPO}/session-state/{live/session-hub-linux.json, session-hub-linux.json}?t=<cachebust>`, no token.
- The file itself already documents (index.html:629-634) that **raw.githubusercontent.com serves edge copies that can be minutes stale**, and that `waitForHub()` therefore switches to the REST contents API after 3 stale reads (`staleReads >= 3`). **`tryOpenLive` has no such fallback.**
- Consequence A: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'ended'` file → prints the exact 01:25:16 message "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" → returns false, even though the hub is live and its address is published. Dead end.
- Consequence B: `tryOpenLive` reads a stale `state:'live'` file holding the PREVIOUS run's dead ngrok URL → probes it → "Failed to fetch" → prints the exact 01:21:03 message "Адрес хаба молчит (туннель мёртв...)" → returns false. Dead end.
- `firstReachableBase(bases, ztOrCandidates, runId)` — index.html:685. Walks bases × token candidates, returns `{base, zt, errors}`; every failure reason is collected in `errors[]`.
- When ALL probes fail with network-class reasons (`/failed to fetch|networkerror|load failed/i`), `tryOpenLive` lines 554-557 concludes "туннель мёртв" and tells the user to press the restart button manually. No automatic action is taken, even though `restartRunner(token, zt, runner)` (index.html:573) and `cancelAndWait(token)` (index.html:527) exist on the very same page and do exactly the needed work.
- `runHubFlow('launch')` lines 1005-1008: when `tryOpenLive` returns false it calls `progFinish(false, 'Доступ не подошёл — хаб закрыт чужим токеном запуска. Нажми «Остановить и перезапустить ранер».')` — i.e. the false diagnosis "чужим токеном" is printed even when the real cause was a dead tunnel or a stale read.
- `openLast()` — index.html:858 — only probes `last.url` and `last.reserve` from localStorage. It never re-reads the session file, so the "Открыть последний (N мин назад)" button can never self-heal. It throws "Последний хаб недоступен: ..." (and via index.html:1318-1319 the generic "Адрес не отвечает — адрес прошлого запуска уже мёртв" text).
- `readSlotRaw(slot)` — index.html:1099 — same raw-only pattern, same ordering hazard: it returns the FIRST path that parses, i.e. `live/session-<slot>.json` always wins over the flat `session-<slot>.json` even if the flat one is newer. Neither function compares `updated_at`/`runId` to pick the freshest.
- `sessionBases(s)` — index.html:842 — order is `s.ngrok`, then `s.hubUrl || s.url`, then `s.url2`.
- `hubCandidates(s)` — index.html:813 — produces token candidates incl. a `spare` derived from the GitHub token via `sha256Hex`.
- `waitForHub(token, sinceMs, sleepMs, cancelled, runId)` — index.html:614 — the good pattern: raw first, API fallback after 3 stale reads, plus `runGone()` to notice external cancellation, 240 iterations.

## What I want from you

Read the file yourself, verify my claims, and produce a **concrete design** — not code, the implementation belongs to `pilot`. Deliver:

1. **Verdict on each of my 6 findings**: confirmed / wrong / partially right, with line numbers and the evidence that settles it.
2. **Any additional critical bug in this same code path that I missed.** Look hard at: stale-vs-fresh session-file selection, the `live/` vs flat path precedence, what happens across a page reload mid-launch (`savePending`/`readPending`/`clearPending` at index.html:728-735 — `clearPending` is called on success at 567 and 958, but is the pending zt ever *used* on a later open?), the auto-lock IIFE at index.html:887-912 (it reads the module-scope `nowMs` — is that ever updated? If `nowMs` is a one-shot value the age math is permanently frozen), and whether `openSlot`'s `tokenNow()` is defined.
3. **The recommended fix design**, in priority order, with the specific functions to change and the exact behavioural contract:
   - How `tryOpenLive` should obtain a fresh session file (reuse the `readHubSession` + stale-detection logic from `waitForHub`? Extract a shared helper? What staleness signal — `updated_at`, `runId` vs the active run's id, or both?).
   - Whether and when auto-restarting the runner is safe. Key safety question: the tunnel may be dead while the run is still alive and doing real work (VNC/repos, hours). A wrong auto-restart kills a healthy run. Propose a concrete gate — e.g. only after the fresh read confirms the address is stale/dead AND a fresh `GET /repos/.../actions/runs/{runId}` confirms the run state — and say exactly what to do when the run is alive but the tunnel is dead (the screenshot-1 case: run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead). Is there a cheaper recovery than a full restart (e.g. reading a fresher session file from a different path, or the reserve base)?
   - Whether `readSlotRaw` should pick the freshest of the two paths instead of the first.
   - What `runHubFlow`'s `progFinish(false, ...)` message should say in each failure mode, given the diagnosis is wrong today.
   - Whether `openLast` should fall back to a fresh session read + probe.
4. **Risks and regressions** of each change: token-safety (the `zt` gate, the spare-token derivation — must not leak or weaken), extra GitHub API quota burn (raw is free, API costs quota; `listActiveRuns` pages up to 5×100 runs), user-visible progress/progress-bar coherence, and offline/failed-network behaviour.
5. **A concrete test plan.** The repo has `TESTING.md` and a `ci/` dir — check what test tooling exists (node? pytest? plain html?) and specify the tests you'd want, with file paths, in the repo's existing style.

Be concrete and cite line numbers. If you think I'm wrong about something, say so bluntly.
I'll read the file myself before judging anything.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Publish the live session's connection details so the panel can show them.
#
# The job summary already prints the address, user and password, but it is
# prose meant for a human with a browser: not machine-readable, and on a phone
# it is several taps behind the Actions UI. The panel is where the session is
# started, so it is where the credentials belong.
#
# They go to an orphan branch, session-state, as session.json. An orphan branch
# keeps this churn out of the history of main and lets the file be replaced
# wholesale every time without ever conflicting.
#
# WHO CAN READ THIS
#   On a public repository the branch is public, and so is the password in it.
#   That is the same exposure as the run summary, which is also public - but it
#   is worth being explicit, because a password on a web page feels different
#   from one in a log. Everything here dies with the runner within six hours,
#   and any secret in it is regenerated per run. If that is not acceptable,
#   make the repository private; the panel reads it with the same token either
#   way.
#

#   file - session-linux.json, session-windows.json, session-agent.json,

#   runners stop overwriting each other); the bare slot stays for old runs.

#   old single session.json is used, which keeps the older workflows working
#   unchanged.
#

history_bucket() {
  local raw="$1" d=""
  if [[ "$raw" =~ ^([0-9]{4})([0-9]{2})([0-9]{2})$ ]]; then

  printf '%s/%s' "$d" "$wd"

  echo "publish_session: published $FILE to $BRANCH"
else
  echo "publish_session: push failed after retries" >&2
  exit 1

#

#   branch that was never migrated keeps working, and a half-migrated branch is
#   still readable. The migration only ever MOVES files (git mv, so history is

#   that appeared after the deploy are skipped (the source no longer exists).

  exit 1

cleanup() { rm -rf "$WORK"; }

  log "no $BRANCH branch yet; nothing to migrate"
  exit 0

move() {
  [ -e "$1" ] || return 0
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" || return 1
  if git mv -q "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null || mv -f "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null; then
    moved=$((moved + 1))
    return 0
  fi
  log "could not move $1 -> $2"
  return 1

  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "live/$f"
done

# 2. the model rosters
for f in models-*.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "models/$f"
done

# 3. the audit/code pair
for f in audit.json code.json; do
  [ -e "$f" ] || continue
  move "$f" "snapshots/$f"
done

#    (saved/<name>-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.json -> history/YYYY-MM-DD/Wd/<name>-<stamp>.json)
if [ -d saved ]; then

    base="$(basename "$f")"
    day=""
    if [[ "$base" =~ ([0-9]{8})T[0-9]{6} ]]; then

  exit 0
fi

git config user.name  "Session state migration"
git commit -q -m "session-state: split the root into live/, models/, snapshots/, history/"

pushed=0
for attempt in $(seq 1 8); do

    break
  fi

  git fetch -q origin "$BRANCH" 2>/dev/null || true
  git rebase -q FETCH_HEAD >/dev/null 2>&1 || git reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD

if [ "$pushed" = 1 ]; then
  log "migrated $moved file(s) into folders on $BRANCH"
  exit 0
fi
log "push failed after retries; the branch is untouched (nothing was force-pushed)"
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reaper: close session slots whose runner is provably gone (Z12).
#
# WHY
#   Every slot in live/ carries the runId that published it. When a run is
#   cancelled or fails, GitHub does NOT reach the `if: always()` steps inside
#   the job - the job dies with the run. So nothing ever flips the slot to
#   ended, and the panel keeps handing out an address that is already dead
#   (Cloudflare answers 1033 on a quick tunnel whose connector is gone).
#
#   Observed: run #242 (completed/cancelled) still published
#   state:"live" with url did-biz-doe-choosing.trycloudflare.com, and
#   session-hub-windows.json still said state:"live" for run #86, which has
#   been completed/failure since 21 Sep.
#
# WHAT IT DOES
#   For every live/session-*.json: read runId, ask the Actions API for that
#   run's status/conclusion, and rewrite the slot with state:"ended" when the
#   run is no longer in_progress/queued/requested/waiting/pending. A run that
#   has already been reaped is left alone (no commit churn).
#
#   It only ever writes to slots that carry a runId, so a slot published by
#   hand (no run) is never touched.
#
# WHY IT IS SAFE TO RUN ANYWHERE
#   It is a separate cron workflow, not part of the hub job, so it works even
#   when every session run is dead - which is exactly when it is needed.

name: NPM Hub

# The third agent: npm-hub on a runner, in a browser tab of the panel.
#
# WHAT IT IS
#   npm-hub/ is a tools dashboard with xterm terminal tabs: it detects the
#   installed AI CLI agents (claude, gemini, codex, copilot, opencode and
#   friends) and opens each in its own terminal session, with a file manager
#   and a live model registry on top. All of that logic already lives in the
#   repo - this workflow optionally preinstalls the CLIs, starts the server and
#   publishes the address, the same way the desks and the other agents do.
#
#   No work branch, no autosave: the hub edits nothing by itself, it is a
#   launcher. What outlives the runner is the models snapshot
#   (models-hub-<os>.json, one per OS) and whatever the user saves through the panel.
#
# AUTH
#   Panel-launched runs carry a gate token (the `token` input, generated per
#   launch): without ?zt= the hub answers 401 on every page, API call and
#   terminal socket. The tunnel address itself stays unguessable and dies

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      os:
        description: "Runner OS"
        type: choice
        options: [linux, windows]
        default: linux
      label:
        description: "Name for this session"
        type: string
        default: "hub"
      token:
        description: "Hub gate token, generated by the panel (empty = no gate)"
        type: string
        default: ""
      gh_token:
        description: "GitHub PAT for the server-side /gh proxy (empty = proxy off)"
        type: string
        default: ""

        description: "Runner for the Linux job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "ubuntu-latest"
      runner_windows:
        description: "Runner for the Windows job (a label, or self-hosted - see pc-local/runner)"
        type: string
        default: "windows-latest"
      preinstall:
        description: "Install all CLI agents at startup (minutes); off = each installs at first click"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      replace:
        description: "Replace an active session run"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff:
        description: "This run takes over a session that another runner handed over"
        type: boolean
        default: false
      handoff_from:
        description: "runId of the runner that handed the session over"
        type: string
        default: ""
      rescue_ssh:
        description: "tmate rescue shell published to session-state control/rescue.json (lifeline when the hub+web die)"
        type: boolean
        default: true
      command_queue:
        description: "safe command queue on session-state control/queue.json (whitelisted ops only)"
        type: boolean
        default: true

concurrency:
  group: zen-panel-session-${{ github.repository }}
  # A handoff run must NOT cancel the runner it takes over from: that runner
  # saves, waits until this one has published itself, and only then steps aside.
  # A manual «заменить» from the panel still cancels the old run.
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ inputs.replace && !inputs.handoff }}

permissions:
  contents: write

env:
  HUB_LOGS: /home/runner/.npm-hub/logs

jobs:
  # ── Hub on Linux ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  hub:
    if: inputs.os == 'linux'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_linux }}
    timeout-minutes: 360

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          path: fork

      # The gate token is echoed into this job's logs by the shell (every
      # x-hub-token probe line). Mask it before anything prints it.
      - name: Mask the gate token in logs
        if: inputs.token != ''
        shell: bash
        env:
          ZT_MASK: ${{ inputs.token }}
          GH_MASK: ${{ inputs.gh_token }}
        run: |
          echo "::add-mask::$ZT_MASK"
          echo "::add-mask::$GH_MASK"

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: "20"

      - name: Restore the npm/pip caches
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.npm
            ~/.cache/pip
          # run_id: every run saves a fresh cache (an exact-key hit would skip
          # the save and the freshly downloaded tarballs would never persist).
          key: hub-pkg-linux-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: hub-pkg-linux-

      - name: Install the CLI agents
        if: inputs.preinstall
        run: |
          # One npm call: its downloads run concurrently, so this is minutes
          # faster than installing one by one. If it fails, fall back to
          # per-package attempts so a renamed package cannot cancel the
          # rest. Whatever lands on PATH the hub picks up; anything missing
          # still launches through `npx -y` at click time.
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true
          PKGS="opencode-ai @anthropic-ai/claude-code @google/gemini-cli @openai/codex @github/copilot @qwen-code/qwen-code http-server"
          npm install -g $PKGS >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 || \
            for p in $PKGS; do npm install -g "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/npm-i.log 2>&1 \
              && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
          pip install --quiet aider-chat goose-ai >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 || \
            for p in aider-chat goose-ai; do pip install --quiet "$p" >$HUB_LOGS/pip-i.log 2>&1 \
              && echo "installed $p" || echo "skipped $p"; done
          echo "--- on PATH now ---"
          for c in opencode claude gemini codex copilot qwen aider goose http-server; do
            command -v "$c" >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "  $c: $(command -v $c)" || echo "  $c: -"
          done

      - name: Install the hub dependencies
        working-directory: fork/npm-hub
        run: npm ci

      - name: Install OpenCode for session recovery
        run: |
          set -e
          echo "$HOME/.opencode/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          export PATH="$HOME/.opencode/bin:$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
          if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash || true
          fi
          if ! command -v opencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            npm install -g opencode-ai
          fi
          command -v opencode
          opencode --version || true

      - name: Put zen-agent on PATH
        run: |
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec node "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/fork/agent/zen-agent.js" "$@"\n' \
            | sudo tee /usr/local/bin/agent >/dev/null
          sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/agent

      - name: Create the work folder and restore repositories
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          export HUB_LOGS="$HOME/.npm-hub/logs"; mkdir -p ~/hub-work "$HUB_LOGS" 2>/dev/null || true; mkdir -p ~/.npm-hub/logs
          echo "logs dir ready $(ls -ld ~/.npm-hub/logs 2>&1 || ls -ld "$HUB_LOGS" 2>&1)"
          if [ "${{ inputs.handoff }}" = "true" ]; then
            echo "::notice::session relay: taking the session over from run ${{ inputs.handoff_from }}. Everything below is a restore of what that runner saved; its watchdog is waiting for this run to publish before it steps aside."
          fi
          # ONE clone of session-state for both restores below.
          #
          # The branch had grown past 70 MB, and each of the two restores
          # cloned all of it - twice - before the hub could publish its
          # address. About 39 MB of that is one uploaded APK under artifacts/
          # that nothing in the restore path ever reads, so the clone carries
          # the same blob filter the script does. Both calls get the tree.
          STATE_DIR="$HOME/.npm-hub/tmp/session-state"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$STATE_DIR")"
          rm -rf "$STATE_DIR"
          STATE_REMOTE="https://x-access-token:${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}@github.com/${{ github.repository }}.git"
          if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:limit=1m --branch session-state \
               "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
            if ! git clone -q --depth 1 --branch session-state \
                 "$STATE_REMOTE" "$STATE_DIR" 2>/dev/null; then
              STATE_DIR=""
              echo "::notice::no session-state branch yet; starting without the saved history"
            fi
          fi

name: Reap dead sessions

on:
  # Instant: a session run that just finished can no longer be serving its
  # tunnel, so its slot must stop claiming to be live. workflow_run fires the
  # moment the run reaches a terminal state - including cancellation, which is

  local id="$1" body status

Confirmed:
- Session descriptor has: kind, os, url, hubUrl, desktop, mobile, auth, tools, label, startedAt, state, runId, runNumber, repo (+ url2, ngrok when the keepers add them). NO `updated_at`. The reaper adds `reapedAt`.

- The sample `session-hub-linux.json` at repo root has no `url2` and no `ngrok` — matching the observed 2 bases.

Now, one more verification: the user's claim that `tryOpenLive` line 542 uses ONLY raw. Confirmed. And "raw.githubusercontent serves stale edge copies" — documented at 629-634. Confirmed.

Let me double-check one thing about `waitForHub`'s staleness logic vs what I'd recommend, and confirm the exact behaviour of the 01:25:16 message. At 01:25:16 the message is "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)…" which is line 544 — printed when `!s || s.state!=='live' || !(s.hubUrl||s.url)`. Given the run is alive and the panel had just been fighting a dead tunnel, the most likely `s` is the reaped `ended` file of a previous run (the reaper flips to ended on run completion, and the file stays ended until the next run publishes). Actually careful: if the run is alive (5h33m, in_progress), the reaper would NOT reap it (run_is_alive → 0 → continue). So the live slot should still say `state:live` with runId 34698442856-ish. Hmm.

But consider the timeline: the run is #385 running 5h33m. Wait — 6h cap. At 01:25 the panel says "Запуск уже идёт, но адрес хаб ещё не сообщил". Two sub-cases:
(a) `s` is null → raw fetch failed (offline) or both paths 404. 
(b) `s.state === 'ended'` → the reaper flipped it. The reaper fires on `workflow_run: completed` for NPM Hub — but that only fires when the run completes. If the run is alive, the reaper wouldn't have touched it. UNLESS the slot on the branch belongs to an OLDER run that ended, and run #385 never got to publish (e.g. it's stuck in "restore repositories" for 5h33m, or the tunnel never came up). The user's screenshot says "#385 running for 5h33m" from the «Последние запуски» card — that card shows ALL recent runs, and the row's tail for in-progress is ' · идёт HH:MM:SS'. So #385 is genuinely in_progress.

If #385 is in_progress but the slot still holds the previous run's (reaped→ended) descriptor, then `s.state==='ended'` → message at 544 → false. That happens when: the new run is alive but hasn't published yet — 5h33m into the run though? That'd be a wedged run. OR the raw edge is serving a *very* stale copy from before the reaper's write.

Either way, both (a) and (b) are handled identically and wrongly: the panel should compare `s.runId` with the active run id it *already fetched*, and if they differ, the file is stale by construction.

I have enough. Let me also quickly double check `hub-shell-test.js` / `panel-tabs-e2e.js` for how they test index.html — no, hub-connect-e2e.js already covers index.html. Good enough for the test plan; I'll extend hub-connect-e2e.js and add a new suite.

One last check: `stopWaiting` reset. In `tryOpenLive` called from `autoPending` (1404) — no progStart, so `stopWaiting` isn't reset; and the IIFE at 887 autoLock may be simultaneously running `openLast()` on a 3s timer. **autoPending and autoLock can both fire ~simultaneously and both navigate** — two racing `location.href` assignments and two probe storms. Real (minor) bug.

Also `autoPending` ignores the result of tryOpenLive and never calls progFinish — fine, but it also doesn't set busy on the launch button, so the user can press «Запустить хаб» while autoPending is probing → concurrent flows. Same class as the prog-stop un-busy bug.

Let me count API cost of the current path for the quota analysis:
- `detectSessionConflict` → `listActiveRuns` → up to 5 pages × per_page=100 = up to 5 requests (usually 1-2).
- `tryOpenLive` → 1-2 raw fetches (free) → `hubCandidates` → `spareToken` (local crypto) → `firstReachableBase` → up to 3 bases × 4 candidates = 12 cross-origin fetches (free, third-party).
So the current stuck loop is cheap in GitHub quota but expensive in *third-party* requests and user time. Adding a fresh API read (1 request) is negligible. Adding auto-restart costs `cancelAndWait` → `waitForRunsToStop` up to 400 requests — that's the quota bomb. Must cap it (e.g. 20 polls × 3 s = 60 s, 20 requests).

Now — the "no manual intervention" requirement. Design:

**Core principle: separate "reconnect" (free, safe, always allowed) from "replace the runner" (destructive, gated).**

Tier 0 (always, silent, no token cost): re-read the session file from BOTH paths and take the freshest; probe all bases × all candidates. Costs 1 raw fetch (free) + up to 12 third-party fetches.
Tier 1 (1 GitHub API call): if the file's runId ≠ the active run's id, or the file looks stale → re-read via the REST contents API (authoritative, costs 1). Repeat the probe.
Tier 2 (0 GitHub API calls, 1 branch write): if the run is alive and every base is dead → enqueue `reopen-tunnel` on `control/queue.json` (1 PUT + 1 GET for the sha), then poll the session file raw (free) for up to ~90 s for a new URL. This repairs the tunnel without touching the run.
Tier 3 (only if Tier 2 fails twice AND `control/heartbeat-hub.json` shows the control daemon is not running, i.e. nothing on the runner can heal): then, and only then, offer/perform the restart. Gate: the run must be the hub run, no other session run active, AND the user has opted in (a persisted "авто-восстановление" switch, default ON but with a hard daily cap, e.g. 3 restarts/day, and a hard rule: never restart a run whose job has been in_progress < 10 min... actually never restart within the first 10 min because the run is still booting — and never if a `handoff` is in progress).

Actually, better: never auto-cancel at all in tier 3 on the first pass. Make tier 3 = "keep the panel alive and honest" (report precisely), and tier 4 = auto-restart, which requires: (a) fresh session read shows the run is gone/ended, (b) `GET /actions/runs/{runId}` confirms status=completed, and (c) the user is not connected. If the run is confirmed completed, restarting is free of data loss — and in that case the panel should NOT restart either, it should just say "the run ended" and offer the button. Auto-restart only makes sense when the run is alive-but-wedged and unrepairable. In that case data loss is a real risk (unsaved work), but there IS a work-backup daemon every 300 s + autoship every 180 s + snapshot every 120 s, so a restart loses at most ~2-5 min of terminal output. That materially lowers the risk and is worth stating: `backup-work.sh` runs every 300 s and `auto-ship.sh` every 180 s per repo. So a restart is far less destructive than the current 6h cap kill.

That's the key safety argument the user asked for. Good.

Let me also verify the claim about `nowMs` one more time and `tokenNow` hoisting — both fine.

One more possible bug to verify: line 826 `if (!seen['']) out.push('');` — `seen` is `{}` and `seen['']` is undefined initially, so it pushes ''. But if a candidate was '' ... `push()` ignores empty values (`if (!k...) return`). So '' is only pushed once. Fine. But `seen` uses a plain object as a map — `seen['constructor']` would be truthy! Not reachable since tokens are hex. OK.

And: `hubCandidates` pushes `pend.zt` — but `savePending` is called AFTER `dispatchHub` (1018-1019) and after `dispatchWorkflow` in `$('run-hub')` (1388 before). Fine.

Now, `clearPending()` on success at 567/958 removes the only record of the launch zt. After a successful open, `saveLast` holds it in the URL. OK. But consider: open succeeds → clearPending → the user reloads → `openLast` uses `lastOriginToken().zt` = the zt from the URL. Fine.

**A real bug though**: `tryOpenLive` at 566 calls `saveLast(url, ...)` then `clearPending()` — but if `location.href` navigation fails silently (WebView blocks), the pending zt is already gone and the only copy lives in `hub_last`. Acceptable.

Now the biggest *architectural* bug I should name: **there is no background reconciler**. Every entry point is a one-shot user action. The panel has no "I'm connected but the tunnel died and I want to be moved to a new address automatically" — because the page navigates away into the hub (location.href at 570/961/1308), and from inside the hub there's no reconnect logic at all in this file. So if the user is sitting in the hub page and the tunnel dies, nothing in the panel brings them back — they're in the hub's own SPA. Let me check whether the hub SPA has any reconnect. `npm-hub/public`? That's a separate deliverable, but worth flagging as scope.

Actually for "AI works automatically without intervention", the essential thing is: the panel app must have a watchdog while it's open. Design: a `watchdog` IIFE at load — every 30 s (raw fetch, free): read the session file; if its runId differs from `hub_last`'s runId, or if the currently-open hub URL fails a preflight, try to migrate to a new base. Only run while the hub tab is the active tab and `document.hidden` is false (so a backgrounded WebView doesn't burn battery). Plus on `visibilitychange`/`online` events → immediate reconcile. That's the self-healing loop.

Let me verify there's no existing watchdog in the file — grep for setInterval occurrences: 277 (prog timer), 898 (lockTimer), 923 (progFillTimer), 1117 (session age ticker). No watchdog. Confirmed.

Confirmed: `restartRunner` (573) is **dead code** — never called. The only caller of the cancel+dispatch logic is the inlined block at 986-998.

I have everything. Now write the answer: concise but complete. Structure per my contract: one-paragraph verdict first, then the required sections. The user asked for 5 specific deliverables, so I'll follow their structure but keep it tight.

Let me be precise about the "additional critical bugs" list, ordered:

1. `describeBaseFailure(bases, probe.errors, candidates[candidates.length-1] || '', !!spare)` at 1302 — the zt arg is always `''` (open gate is always last, 826) → openSlot ALWAYS prints "Нет токена запуска (zt): адрес отвечает 401" even when a launch token existed and the hub rejected it. Wrong diagnosis, guaranteed. Also makes branches 712-714 unreachable dead code.

2. `restartRunner` at 573 is dead — the restart path is duplicated inline at 986-998. Two copies of a destructive operation; fixing one doesn't fix the other.

3. `detectSessionConflict` (532) throws away the run object; `tryOpenLive` then guesses staleness from a file it can't authenticate. `s.runId` vs the active run's id is a free, decisive staleness signal that is already in hand. Also `preflightHub` already returns `j.runId` (672) so the server itself can arbitrate.

4. `readHubSessionRaw` swallows the difference between "no file" and "no network" → `!s` prints "адрес хаб ещё не сообщил (или он уже выключен)" at 544. Offline phone = nonsense diagnosis. `readHubSession` (609) already has the raw→API fallback that fixes it; tryOpenLive just doesn't call it.

5. No timeouts anywhere: `api()` (322), `readHubSessionRaw` (594), `preflightHub` (667). A hung TCP connect blocks the probe loop indefinitely — in an auto-recovery watchdog that means the watchdog wedges forever and stops healing. Must be `AbortSignal.timeout(8000-12000)`.

6. Concurrency: `prog-stop` (1032-1038) un-greys the buttons at 1037 while the flow is still awaiting → a second `runHubFlow` can start and both will `location.href`. Also `progAbort` (280) is created and never passed to any fetch → "Прервать ожидание" doesn't actually abort anything. Also `autoPending` (1396) fires `tryOpenLive` unawaited with no button lock, racing `autoLock`'s 3 s `openLast()` (900). Any auto-recovery loop makes these races routine instead of rare → need a single-flight mutex.

7. The unused remote-repair channel: `control/queue.json` + `reopen-tunnel`/`restart-hub`/`up-hub` ops (hub_control.sh 22, 87-135) + `control/heartbeat-hub.json` (2-min census). The panel has zero references (grep). This is the correct self-heal for "run alive, tunnel dead" and it's already implemented and whitelisted on the runner.

8. `openLast` uses a single token (`lastOriginToken().zt`) — no pending, no spare. Even with a fresh session file it would 401.

9. `ngrok` leg absent in the user's run (2 bases = one "пробую резервный" line) → the third failure domain wasn't there. Either NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty (hub.yml prints "::notice::NGROK_AUTHTOKEN secret is empty - the ngrok reserve leg is off") or the keeper failed. Diagnostic hint for the pilot to check the run log.

10. Quota: `waitForRunsToStop` default 400 attempts × 3 s (513-524) and `followRun` 90×2 (422-453) and the fire-and-forget at 942 — if auto-restart goes live, budget it.

Now the design. Let me write the contract precisely.

P0 — one shared, authenticated, honest session read:
`readSessionFresh(token, opts)` → returns `{ s, src, err }` where `src ∈ {'raw','api','none'}` and `err` distinguishes `offline` / `notfound` / `unauthorized` / `http`. Implement by: fetch BOTH paths via raw, keep both parsed results (not first-wins), pick the one with the greater `Date.parse(startedAt)`, tie-break on `runNumber`; if the winner disagrees with `activeRunId`, do ONE `readHubSessionViaApi` and prefer that. Return `null` only when both are genuinely absent.

Change `readHubSessionRaw` → `readHubSessionPathsRaw` (collect both), keep `readHubSessionRaw` as a thin wrapper so `readHubSession` (609) and existing tests keep working.

P1 — `tryOpenLive(token, activeRun)`:
- `detectSessionConflict` returns `{ kind, run }` instead of a string; line 1002-1008 updated. This is the single most valuable 3-line change.
- read fresh; if `!s` → say "не вижу файла сессии" and offer to re-check, NOT "туннель мёртв".
- if `s.runId && activeRun && String(s.runId) !== String(activeRun.id)` → the file belongs to a dead run: report "файл сессии от прошлого рана #N; текущий #M ещё не опубликовал адрес" and, if `activeRun.status` is active, fall into the wait/repair path instead of giving up.
- if `s.state !== 'live'` → do NOT return false immediately; check the run first.
- probe; on full network-class failure → call the repair ladder instead of printing "нажмите кнопку".

P2 — repair ladder (`recoverLive(token, s, run)`), returns `{ ok, base, url, action }`:
 1. Re-read via API once; re-probe. (1 quota)
 2. `enqueueControl(token, 'reopen-tunnel', 'hub')` — PUT `control/queue.json` `{seq: now, op, target:'hub', from:'panel'}`; needs the current sha (GET). Then poll raw every 10 s for up to 120 s for a changed `url`/`ngrok`; on change, re-probe. (2 quota, 0 destructive)
 3. If `control/heartbeat-hub.json` is missing/stale > 6 min → the runner can't self-heal; only NOW consider restart, and even then only via `restartRunner` (573) — never inline — with the gate below.

Gate for step 3 (all must hold): `isHubRun(run)`; no non-hub session run active (`listActiveRuns(isSessionRun)`); `GET /actions/runs/{runId}` returns `status` in ACTIVE_RUN_STATUSES **and** the same check 60 s later (two confirmations, so a transient API blip can't trigger it); user opt-in flag `hub_autorepair === '1'` in localStorage; a restart budget of ≤3 per 24 h persisted in localStorage; and never within the first 10 min of a run's life.

Honest answer to "run alive 5h33m, tunnel dead": with the ladder in place, the answer is step 2 — reopen the tunnel on the live runner, which keeps the run, the repos, the terminals and the 5h33m of session alive, and republishes a fresh URL within ~30 s. A restart is the last resort, and by then the work-backup (300 s) and auto-ship (180 s) daemons bound the loss.

P3 — `runHubFlow` messages (1012). Replace the single false diagnosis with a small enum returned by tryOpenLive: `'opened' | 'no-file' | 'stale-file' | 'still-booting' | 'dead-tunnel' | 'token-mismatch' | 'run-gone'`, each with its own sentence, and `progFinish(false, text)` with that sentence.
